subject: Proposed MAP & cost sanity checks — Redwood + Acme
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Joe Barnes <joe.barnes@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700 (PDT)
Subject: Proposed MAP & cost sanity checks — Redwood + Acme

Hi Joe / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great questions on latency and rollout. I put together an initial mutual action plan (MAP) focused on two things you asked for: (1) an evaluation plan we can run during POC, and (2) a short cost sanity check so you have a realistic tokens/$ view for budgeting.

High-level proposed MAP milestones (timeline suggestion):
- Week 0: Sign MAP (legal + procurement)
- Weeks 1–2: Eval run (50k sample prompts, 3 model configs)
- Weeks 3–4: Performance tuning (caching + batching profiles)
- Week 5: Finalize SLA & pricing for Dedicated pool

For the cost sanity checks I want to validate a few assumptions with you:
- Average tokens per request (user prompt + expected assistant)
- Hit rate for prefix/KV caching on repeat prompts
- Batching target (max latency allowed vs throughput)

If you’re OK I’ll attach a compact cost workbook and a sample eval prompt set so we can lock numbers by the end of next week. Would you prefer the eval to focus on (A) customer-facing chat flows or (B) back-office summarization?

Next steps: reply with preferred eval focus and an internal contact for procurement/legal redlines. I’ll loop in our solutions lead and pricing engineer to validate numbers.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_outline.md (text, 8KB)]

Joe —

Attached: MAP_v2_ACME.xlsx (compact cost workbook), eval_prompt_set.json (50k sample seeds), cost_assumptions.md (assumptions & sensitivity). High-level highlights from the workbook:

Assumptions we used (please confirm / edit in the workbook):
- Avg tokens per end-to-end request (prompt + response): 420 tokens
- Expected repeat-hit rate (prefix/KV cache): 28% baseline, sensitivity +/− 10pp
- Batching targets: 1–4 concurrent requests per batch for latency-sensitive flows (p50 target), up to 12 requests/batch for background processing
- Two model configs: medium (1.3B quantized) and large (7B quantized); hosted price used is market rate + Redwood margin

Representative unit economics (example rows from workbook):
- Hosted medium: $12 per 1M tokens (base), after caching effective cost ~ $8.6 per 1M tokens at 28% cache hit
- Dedicated large: $6 per 1M tokens (committed) assuming sustained batching and 70% GPU utilization

Notes on tradeoffs:
- Caching gives the largest swing for conversational apps with repeated prompts; a small increase in hit rate (e.g., 28% -> 38%) reduces marginal token cost by ~15% in our model.
- Batching improves throughput but increases tail latency; we show two operating points in the workbook you can toggle.

Requested next steps:
1) You confirm the avg tokens/request and whether caching profile above matches production expectations.
2) We run the 50k eval (customer chat flows) next week and ship a short dashboard of quality + cost.
3) If numbers look OK, we lock commit levels for Dedicated and finalize contract language.

Attachments:
- [Attachment: MAP_v2_ACME.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)]

- [Attachment: cost_assumptions.md (text, 6KB)]

Thanks — looping Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (pricing) to validate the workbook details.

Best,
Dylan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Joe Barnes <joe.barnes@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & cost sanity checks — Redwood + Acme

Thanks for the workbook, Dylan — a couple of quick comments after a fast pass: 

- Eval metrics: please add per-prompt pass/fail for business-critical intents (we can provide 12 golden prompts) and a latency SLA curve (p50/p90/p99) at two batching configs.
- Sampling: include warm and cold session segments to show real cache uplift (we recommend a 60/40 split warm:cold for Acme).
- Risk: add an early-fallback policy in the MAP (if model quality drops >5% on golden set, fallback to previous model or increase decode temp).

Karthik — can you confirm the quantization + throughput assumptions? Specifically:
- Do we assume INT8 quantized medium/large? What throughput uplift per GPU do you expect at p50 with batching=4?

Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Replying inline:
> Do we assume INT8 quantized medium/large? What throughput uplift per GPU do you expect at p50 with batching=4?

We should assume INT8 quant for the medium; for the large we model both int8 and 4-bit paths — workbook currently shows conservative INT8 benefits (~1.8–2.3x throughput vs FP16 depending on kernel). At batching=4 p50 we model ~2.0x throughput uplift for medium and ~1.6x for large (quantization + kernel optimizations). Those are conservative — I can attach a microbench sheet if helpful.

Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
